text:
maria: Heads-up — after the branch merge we pushed this morning I'm seeing a noticeable decode p95/tail regression on CI canary. Short-seq workloads worst affected.

devin: yep, noticed the same in dashboards. p95 shortseq +28% vs yesterday baseline. Traces show more time in the decode path.

perf-bot: CI perf-check: job=canary-shortseq, metric=decode_p95, delta=+8.7% (regression threshold exceeded) :rotating_light:

ryan: dug into perf profile on the canary instance. The hot path has shifted to `attn_fused_v2` after the fused-op scheduler refactor. Attn kernel self-time ~78% of CPU sample vs previously ~42%. KV-prefetching also shows increased memcpy/backpressure in the scheduler.

ryan: quick stack excerpt from perf report:
```
attn_fused_v2  78.2%
kv_batch_prefetch  9.5%
scheduler::dispatch 6.1%
decode::emit_tokens 4.8%
```

devin: interesting — the scheduler change in PR #4820 touched the batching heuristic and prefetch thresholds. I ran an A/B with the old heuristic and the hotpath is back to previous distribution.

maria: can we bisect to the exact commit? If it's PR #4820 we should consider a rollback candidate. Canary flagged a rollout hold.

ryan: bisect narrowed it down to commit `abc1234` (fused-scheduler: adjust prefetch threshold & allow larger batch packs). Reproduces locally with unit perf harness. KV eviction rate jumps after that change (eviction_rate: 0.5% -> 12.3%).

devin: eviction thrash means more cache misses -> more attention kernel work for early tokens -> decode tail blows up. Makes sense.

canary-bot: Canary rollout status: PAUSED (hold). Reason: perf regression on canary-shortseq.

maria: ok. Options: 1) revert PR #4820 now to restore baseline, 2) hotfix kernel selector to avoid choosing `attn_fused_v2` on shortseq until prefetch stabilizes, 3) tune prefetch thresholds (temp). Thoughts?

oncall: we should also add an alert that ties eviction rate >5% + p95 delta >10% so it surfaces earlier. I'll file a follow-up.

ryan: I can prototype a defensive kernel-fallback: if shortseq and kv_hit_rate < 90% then prefer `attn_scalar_v1` (more stable). Patch is small. If that reduces p95 we can avoid a full revert.

devin: prefer a revert for safety if timeline is tight. But try ryan's fallback while we open the revert PR. If fallback works we'll keep it and re-land scheduler refactor with tighter checks.

maria: plan: @ryan implement fallback and run canary A/B; @devin open revert PR for #4820 labeled `revert: emergency` and ping infra for expedited review. @oncall add eviction+perf alert. We'll regroup in 30m.

perf-bot: created issue perf/4820-regression (labels: perf, rollback-candidate). CI perf-check will re-run once revert/fallback PRs land.

maria: thanks everyone. Keep updates here with short results. If fallback doesn't cut it by EOD, we'll revert. :thumbsup:
